title: On Combining the two methods into one
subtitle: 科学探索 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 科学探索（科学与技术·科学精神、科学探究）
meta: 主题语境：科学探索（科学与技术·科学精神、科学探究）　|　核心词汇：combine　|　正文 341 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 combine 的形式与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1973 the postman ① combined the two methods into one at once, and every sender in the office said it was the first time anybody had done such a thing there. Three weeks on, people still spoke of how quietly it was done and of how, ever since, the postman ② combines the two methods into one in the rain without being asked. My mother said later that to ③ combine the two methods into one at all was the part nobody had expected.

By then somebody had surely ④ combined the two methods into one before — a line in the list for June 1967 hints at it — but nobody could name the person. ⑤ Combining the two methods into one at once, the postman said once, is nine parts patience and one part nerve; it is not the doing of it that people remember.

My uncle, who kept the envelope at the far box, meant the other thing entirely. He said that if anybody should ever ⑥ combine patience with great speed in the rain, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again. The rule the old hands handed down was plainer still: ⑦ Combine patience with great speed at once and never mention it again.

By 1980 the whole business had shrunk to half a line in the list, and a new sender from the next office ⑧ combines patience with great speed at once every week without once asking what it had cost the first time. My mother, who had watched all of it from the box, said nothing at all; she simply ⑨ combined the two methods into one again when nobody else would.

⑩ To combine the two methods into one, my mother said in 1985, is not one thing but two: what you do and what the office remembers of it. She said the second half never grows lighter, and nowadays, whenever the office forgets, somebody combines the two methods into one in the rain again and somebody must combine the two methods into one at once all over again.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. v. 结合（一般过去式 combined the two methods into one：1973 年邮差头一回这样做，二话不说地）
B. v. 结合（一般现在 combines the two methods into one：自那以后成了老习惯，不必有人开口）
C. v. 结合（不定式 to combine the two methods into one：文中两处，一是母亲说的“难就难在……”，一是结尾那句格言）
D. v. 结合（过去完成时 had combined the two methods into one：1967 年六月的收发清单上那行字之前就有人做过）
E. v. 结合（动名词 combining the two methods into one 作主语：“九分耐心、一分胆气”那一句）
F. v. 兼有（combine patience with great speed：should ever 之后的原形，指万一真要去兼有既有耐心又快得出奇）
G. v. 兼有（combine patience with great speed：祈使句，转述老手们当年立下的那条规矩）
H. v. 结合（后段两处：新来的寄信人照例 combines patience with great speed，而母亲又一次 combined the two methods into one）

answers.why: combine 意为“结合”，1973 年邮差二话不说地结合把两套办法合成一套，那是邮局里头一回有人肯这么做，故用一般过去式 combined。
combine 意为“结合”，自那以后邮差淋着雨把这件事做了一遍又一遍，不必有人开口，故用一般现在 combines。
combine 意为“结合”，母亲说的是“难就难在肯结合把两套办法合成一套”，此处为不定式 to combine the two methods into one。
combine 意为“结合”，收发清单里 六月 那行字说明早在 1980 年之前就有人结合过，故用过去完成时 had combined。
combine 意为“结合”，邮差说“结合把两套办法合成一套这件事是九分耐心一分胆气”，此处 combining the two methods into one 作主语。
combine 意为“兼有”，叔叔说的是“万一真有人去兼有既有耐心又快得出奇”，should ever 之后用原形 combine patience with great speed。
combine 意为“兼有”，老手们留下的规矩是祈使句：立刻兼有既有耐心又快得出奇（combine patience with great speed at once），以后再也不要提起。
combine 意为“结合”，新来的寄信人每个星期都照例兼有既有耐心又快得出奇，从不问头一回的代价，用一般现在 combines。
combine 意为“结合”，母亲在无人肯做的时候又一次二话不说地结合把两套办法合成一套，用一般过去式 combined 叙述。
combine 意为“结合”，结尾那句是母亲 1985 年的话：要结合把两套办法合成一套，其实不是一件事，而是两件事——你做的那一件，和邮局记住的那一件。

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 combine 的 3 种不同形式（过去式、第三人称、-ing、不定式等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1973 the postman combined the two methods into one at once, and nobody in the office forgot it.
Even now the postman combines the two methods into one in the rain whenever the office asks.
Combining the two methods into one at once, my mother used to say, is nine parts patience and one part nerve.
If anybody should ever combine patience with great speed in the rain, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again.
A new sender from the next office combines patience with great speed at once every week, asking nothing about the past.
When nobody else would, my mother combined the two methods into one again, and the office remembered that half.
